modules.acceptance: Employee records, assignments, employment state, attachments, scope, and audit are plugin-owned.
Customers, suppliers, contacts, addresses, settlement, and qualification links share one scoped party model.
Products, SKUs, dosage forms, specifications, units, categories, and manufacturers are governed master data.
Evidence, reviews, validity, expiry alerts, and business gates use owned files and host jobs.
General OA documents use host numbering, forms, documents, workflow, files, comments, and timeline.
Contacts, visits, opportunities, follow-ups, reminders, ownership, and pipeline history remain scoped.
Purchasing and receiving enforce approval, qualification, quantity, price, idempotency, and audit rules.
Sales, allocation, picking, and delivery enforce customer, stock, lot, expiry, and cancellation rules.
Warehouses, locations, lots, expiry, movements, returns, transfers, and counts form an immutable ledger.
Inspection, quarantine, release, rejection, complaint, and recall decisions are traceable and block invalid stock.
Receivables, payables, invoices, payments, aging, and export reconcile against accepted business documents.
Role-aware dashboards and exports derive only from trusted scoped records.

acceptanceScenarios.result: Build, package, verify, install, start, and health-check the plugin without modifying host production source.
Every module, document type, event, table, route, and permission resolves from one current manifest family.
Backend code imports public pluginclient contracts and no Skoll internal package.
Foundation migration applies and rolls back completely on a clean plugin datastore.
Host bootstrap contains no medical OA factory, service construction, fixture, or unconditional registration.
